title: Rafael Calderon Fournier Wins Presidency for PUSC
description: Rafael Angel Calderon Fournier of the Social Christian Unity Party won the February 1990 presidential election, defeating the PLN candidate. His administration pursued neoliberal economic reforms including trade liberalization and banking privatization.

title: Oscar Arias Awarded Nobel Peace Prize Legacy Shapes Foreign Policy
description: Following his 1987 Nobel Peace Prize for the Esquipulas II peace accords, Arias's legacy continued to shape Costa Rica's identity as a regional peacemaker. The country leveraged its demilitarized status and peace brand in international diplomacy throughout the 1990s.

title: Costa Rica Ratifies UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
description: Costa Rica became an early signatory and ratifier of the UNFCCC, cementing its reputation as an environmental leader. This commitment built on the country's pioneering national parks system and positioned it as a global voice on biodiversity conservation.

title: Jose Maria Figueres Olsen Elected President
description: PLN candidate Jose Maria Figueres, son of the founder of modern Costa Rican democracy, won the 1994 presidential election. His administration shifted toward a more social-democratic agenda, investing in education and technology sectors.

title: Forestry Law Establishes Payment for Environmental Services
description: Costa Rica enacted Forestry Law No. 7575 which created the pioneering Payments for Environmental Services program, compensating landowners for reforestation and conservation. The program became a globally recognized model for market-based environmental policy.

title: Constitutional Amendment Bans Presidential Reelection
description: The Legislative Assembly approved a constitutional amendment prohibiting presidential reelection, reflecting concerns about political dynasty after decades of alternating two-party rule. This ban would later be overturned by the Supreme Court in 2003.

title: Miguel Angel Rodriguez Wins Presidency
description: PUSC candidate Miguel Angel Rodriguez Echeverria won the 1998 presidential election, continuing the two-party alternation pattern. His pro-market administration pursued telecom and energy privatization that would spark major public resistance.

title: Combo ICE Protests Block Telecom Privatization
description: Massive street protests erupted against the 'Combo ICE' bill that would have privatized the state telecommunications and electricity monopoly. The government was forced to withdraw the legislation, marking a major victory for civil society against neoliberal reform.

title: Two-Party System Collapses in Historic Election
description: The 2002 election shattered Costa Rica's stable PLN-PUSC two-party system when the new Citizens Action Party won 14 legislative seats. Abel Pacheco of PUSC won the presidency in an unprecedented runoff as no candidate reached 40 percent.

title: Supreme Court Overturns Presidential Reelection Ban
description: The Constitutional Chamber of the Supreme Court struck down the 1969 amendment banning presidential reelection, ruling it unconstitutional. The decision cleared the way for former president Oscar Arias to seek a second non-consecutive term.

title: Three Former Presidents Accused of Corruption
description: Three former presidents were accused of accepting bribes: Rafael Calderon, Miguel Angel Rodriguez, and Jose Maria Figueres. The scandal devastated the PUSC party and shattered public trust in the traditional political establishment.

title: Oscar Arias Wins Razor-Thin Presidential Election
description: Nobel laureate Oscar Arias narrowly won the presidency with just 40.9 percent against Otton Solis's 39.8 percent, despite polls showing a 12-point lead. The month-long recount highlighted deep polarization over free trade and neoliberal economic policy.

title: CAFTA Approved in First-Ever National Referendum
description: Costa Rica held its first national referendum on October 7, 2007, narrowly approving the Central American Free Trade Agreement with 51.6 percent in favor. The campaign was deeply divisive, with allegations of employer coercion and interference marring the process.

title: Costa Rica Switches Diplomatic Recognition from Taiwan to China
description: President Arias announced Costa Rica was breaking nearly 60 years of diplomatic ties with Taiwan to recognize the People's Republic of China. Costa Rica became the first Central American country to make the switch, driven by growing trade ties with Beijing.

title: CAFTA Implementation Legislation Package Enacted
description: Following the referendum, the Legislative Assembly passed the 13 implementation laws required to bring CAFTA into effect before the March 2008 deadline. The legislation opened telecommunications and insurance markets to competition for the first time.

title: Costa Rica Achieves Carbon Neutrality Pledge
description: Costa Rica announced an ambitious goal to become the world's first carbon-neutral country by 2021, later extended to 2050. The pledge leveraged the country's near-complete renewable electricity generation and extensive forest cover recovery.

title: Laura Chinchilla Elected First Female President
description: Laura Chinchilla of the PLN won with 47 percent of the vote, becoming Costa Rica's first female president. Her election was seen as a continuation of the Arias administration's centrist economic policies.

title: Nicaragua Occupies Disputed Isla Portillos Territory
description: Nicaragua sent military forces into the disputed Isla Portillos area at the mouth of the San Juan River, claiming sovereignty over the wetland territory. Costa Rica, having no army, filed suit at the International Court of Justice in November 2010.

title: ICJ Orders Provisional Measures in Nicaragua Border Dispute
description: The International Court of Justice ordered both Costa Rica and Nicaragua to refrain from sending personnel to the disputed territory near the San Juan River. The ruling was a significant diplomatic victory for Costa Rica's strategy of legal rather than military resolution.

title: China-Funded National Stadium Inaugurated
description: Costa Rica inaugurated a new $100 million national stadium funded and built by China as a gift following the 2007 diplomatic switch. The project symbolized the growing Chinese economic influence in Central America.

title: Major Earthquake Strikes Nicoya Peninsula
description: A 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck the Nicoya Peninsula on September 5, 2012, the strongest in Costa Rica in over a century. Despite the magnitude, casualties were minimal due to strict building codes, though infrastructure damage was significant.

title: Constitutional Court Voids Chinchilla Concession Mining Ban
description: The Constitutional Chamber reviewed challenges to the 2010 moratorium on open-pit mining, navigating tensions between environmental protection and economic development. Costa Rica maintained strict restrictions on mining operations, reinforcing its green economy identity.

title: Luis Guillermo Solis Wins Landslide Anti-Corruption Election
description: Citizens Action Party candidate Luis Guillermo Solis won a landslide second-round victory with 78 percent, capitalizing on deep anti-establishment sentiment. His election marked the first time neither the PLN nor PUSC held the presidency since 1948.

title: ICJ Rules in Favor of Costa Rica in Nicaragua Border Case
description: The International Court of Justice ruled that Costa Rica held sovereignty over the disputed territory of Isla Portillos and that Nicaragua had violated Costa Rican territorial integrity. Nicaragua was ordered to pay compensation for environmental damage caused by its dredging operations.

title: Costa Rica Achieves Over 98 Percent Renewable Electricity
description: Costa Rica generated over 98 percent of its electricity from renewable sources, primarily hydropower, for 299 consecutive days. The achievement attracted global attention and reinforced the country's eco-tourism and green development brand.

title: Pension System Reform Debate Intensifies
description: Growing fiscal pressures prompted intensified debate over reforms to the national pension system managed by CCSS. Actuarial studies warned the disability, old age and death fund could face insolvency without parametric changes, sparking public sector union opposition.

title: Inter-American Court Orders Costa Rica to Legalize Same-Sex Marriage
description: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights issued an advisory opinion that OAS member states must guarantee equal marriage rights to same-sex couples. The ruling had binding force in Costa Rica and set a timeline for legalization.

title: Carlos Alvarado Wins Presidency in Marriage Equality Election
description: PAC candidate Carlos Alvarado defeated evangelical conservative Fabricio Alvarado in a runoff defined by the same-sex marriage debate. The election result was seen as a rejection of religious conservatism and an endorsement of progressive social policy.

title: Massive Public Sector Strike Against Fiscal Reform
description: Public sector workers launched the largest strike in 20 years starting September 2018, protesting a tax reform bill that introduced VAT and cut benefits. The three-month strike caused an estimated 138 billion colones in losses before unions conceded in December.

title: Fiscal Strengthening Law Enacted Despite Protests
description: The Legislative Assembly passed the Ley de Fortalecimiento de las Finanzas Publicas in December 2018, replacing the sales tax with a VAT and imposing spending caps. The law was the most significant fiscal reform in decades, aimed at reducing a deficit exceeding 6 percent of GDP.

title: ICJ Awards Costa Rica Compensation in Nicaragua Dispute
description: The International Court of Justice ordered Nicaragua to pay Costa Rica $378,890.59 in compensation for environmental damage to the disputed wetland territory. The judgment closed a chapter of the border dispute that had persisted since 2010.

title: Costa Rica Joins OECD as First Central American Member
description: Costa Rica formally acceded to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development on May 25, 2021, after an accession process that began in 2015. The membership required extensive institutional and regulatory reforms across taxation, competition, and governance.

title: Same-Sex Marriage Legalized
description: Costa Rica became the first Central American country to legalize same-sex marriage on May 26, 2020, following the Inter-American Court ruling. The landmark change took effect automatically after the court-mandated deadline expired.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Tourism Economy
description: Costa Rica's tourism sector, accounting for roughly 8 percent of GDP, was severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and border closures. The government implemented a phased reopening strategy and border controls that were praised as measured compared to regional peers.

title: Anti-IMF Loan Protests and Road Blockades
description: Weeks of protests erupted in late September 2020 against a proposed $1.7 billion IMF loan that would require new tax measures and spending cuts. Demonstrators set up over 30 road blockades nationwide, leading to clashes with police and dozens of detentions.

title: Tropical Storm Eta and Hurricane Iota Cause Severe Flooding
description: Back-to-back tropical storms Eta and Iota struck in November 2020, causing catastrophic flooding and landslides across Costa Rica. Thousands were displaced and agricultural losses were extensive, compounding the economic damage from the pandemic.

title: Costa Rica Formally Joins OECD
description: Costa Rica officially became the 38th member of the OECD on May 25, 2021, the first Central American nation to join. Accession required reforms to anti-corruption frameworks, public governance, taxation, and environmental regulation.

title: Public Employment Framework Law Enacted
description: The Legislative Assembly passed the Marco de Empleo Publico law to standardize public sector compensation and reduce wage inequality between government workers. The reform was a key condition for OECD accession and sparked union opposition over potential salary reductions.

title: Rodrigo Chaves Wins Presidency as Anti-Establishment Populist
description: Former World Bank economist Rodrigo Chaves of the Social Democratic Progress Party won the April 2022 runoff with 53 percent against ex-president Jose Maria Figueres. His victory represented a sharp rejection of traditional parties and institutional politics.

title: Chaves Declares State of Emergency Over Cost of Living
description: President Chaves declared a state of national emergency over rising living costs shortly after taking office in May 2022. The decree allowed the government to bypass normal procurement procedures and implement emergency price controls on basic goods.

title: Chaves Jaguar Plan Clashes with Legislature and Comptroller
description: President Chaves pushed his Jaguar development plan seeking to limit the Comptroller General's oversight powers and accelerate public contracting. The proposal triggered institutional conflict as the legislature blocked most of his 70 submitted bills.

title: Eco-Tourism Sector Recovers to Record Visitor Numbers
description: Costa Rica's tourism industry rebounded strongly from the pandemic, with international arrivals surpassing pre-COVID levels. The eco-tourism model, anchored by the national parks system covering 25 percent of territory, remained central to economic recovery.

title: Chaves Administration Faces Press Freedom Criticism
description: International press freedom organizations criticized President Chaves's confrontational rhetoric against media, including calling journalists derogatory terms. The pattern of delegitimizing institutional checks raised concerns about democratic erosion in the traditionally stable democracy.

title: Nicaragua Migration Surge Strains Social Services
description: Costa Rica continued to absorb a significant influx of Nicaraguan migrants fleeing the Ortega regime's political repression. The country hosted over 200,000 Nicaraguan asylum seekers, straining public health and education services in border regions.

title: Costa Rica Hosts Transit Migration from South America
description: Costa Rica faced growing challenges as a transit country for migrants traveling from South America through Central America toward the United States. The government negotiated bilateral agreements to manage migration flows through its territory.
